title: Maximum Hamming Distances
summary: For an array nums and integer m, where each nums[i] is less than 2^m, generate an answer array of the same length.
statement: For an array nums and integer m, where each nums[i] is less than 2^m, generate an answer array of the same length. Each answer[i] indicates the greatest bit difference between nums[i] and any other element in nums.
constraints: m is positive and every nums value lies from zero through 2^m-1.
For each occurrence, find the maximum Hamming distance to any value occurring in nums; comparing with itself is allowed.
Return the distances in original input order.
hints: Distance(x,y)=m-distance(complement(x),y), so maximizing distance to the input set equals m minus the complement’s nearest-set distance.
Multi-source BFS from every input value across the m-bit hypercube computes all nearest distances.
Seed distinct nums at distance zero; flip each bit in BFS; answer m-dist[x xor allOnes].
Hypercube path length is Hamming distance, and complementing x converts agreement with x into disagreement bit by bit.

tests.explanation: The farthest listed values differ from 9 in two bits and from 12 or 11 in three bits, giving [2,3,2,3].
Zero and seven differ in all three bits, so both answers are three.
